subject: Re: Embeddings model fit validation — next steps & benchmark links
messages:
From: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@acmeretail.com>

Date: 2026-08-10T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / embedding needs

Thanks for the call today, Marcus. A few clarifications on our side so the follow-up is actionable:
- Our catalog is ~1.2M SKUs; product descriptions vary between ~50-600 chars.
- Primary use cases: short-query semantic search (1-4 words) and product-to-product similarity for recommendations.
- Current infra: FAISS index, 384-d vectors, batched nightly updates.
- Pain: recent category drift (seasonal styles) and drop in top-5 recall for some categories.

Can you send recommended embedding models to test, suggested evaluation metrics (MRR, recall@k, cosine thresholds), and an idea of sample size you need to validate model fit? Also please include any prompt sets / query samples that will help us reproduce.

Looking to move quickly — ideally a short pilot next week.

Best,
Sofia
Customer Success Manager
Acme Retail
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@acmeretail.com>, Ben Turner <b.turner@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings model fit validation — next steps & benchmark links

Great to meet you both earlier — thanks for the context, Sofia. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

Recap of needs:
- High precision for short queries + robust product-product similarity (recommendations).
- Address seasonal/category drift and monitor regressions.
- Keep runtime + index cost reasonable (FAISS currently).

Recommended evaluation plan (pilot):
1) Sample: 50k representative SKUs (stratified by category and seasonality). We can run ~5k query prompts (mix of short queries and long-tail queries) you already have.
2) Models to benchmark (initial):
   - sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2 (768d) — good strong baseline for semantic search
   - all-MiniLM-L12-v2 (384d) — lower-cost baseline, faster indexing
   - rwd-embed-1024 (our quantized 1024-d prod candidate) — better capture of fine-grained semantics at higher dimensionality and cost
3) Metrics: MRR, recall@1/5/10, precision@k, and pairwise cosine distributions (to inspect separation). Also track index size and average query latency.
4) Drift/regression checks: run the same eval across month-over-month snapshots (we can do a before/after seasonal slice). Set a quality regression alert threshold (e.g., >5% drop in recall@5).

Deliverables we’ll provide:
- Eval notebook + scripts (Colab/Drive link) to reproduce.
- CSV with embeddings & nearest neighbor tables for easy inspection (we'll attach).
- Recommendation: if 384-d baselines are too close in quality, consider 768/1024 for categories that require fine-grained discrimination.

Next steps / asks from you:
- Share a 50k SKU sample (CSV with sku_id, title, description, category, season tag).
- Share 1-2k representative queries (short-query focus) and any labeled relevance judgments if available.

Timeline: We can run an initial benchmark in 48–72 hours after we receive the sample + queries. I’ll loop Marissa and Dev for the run.

I attached a short eval CSV template and prompt set (prompt-sets.zip).

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min follow-up if it's easier to align.

—
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-11T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Embeddings model fit validation — infra notes

Quick tech notes for the benchmark run: 
- Indexing: keep FAISS IVFPQ for 384d/768d prototypes; for 1024d recommend HNSW (memory permitting) or IVFPQ with tuned nlist/nprobe.
- Recall vs latency: 1024d vectors will increase index size ~2.5-3x vs 384d; expect higher memory footprint and slightly higher query time unless we increase shards.
- Quantization: we can try 8-bit quantized vectors for rwd-embed-1024 to reduce storage; check quantization impact on cosine separation in the eval.
- Suggested eval hardware: single GPU for embedding generation (T4/GPU), CPU nodes for FAISS build.

I’ll stand by to provision the run; LMK whether we should include hybrid dense+bm25 rerank in the pilot (usually helps short queries).

- Dev
Lead Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Embeddings model fit validation — initial run results (attach)

Uploading a very small smoke-run summary so you can preview format. Attached: eval-results-20260810.csv (top-N metrics by category). Highlights from the smoke run (50k sample, 5k queries):
- all-mpnet-base-v2 (768d): recall@5 = 0.72 overall; MRR = 0.48
- all-MiniLM-L12-v2 (384d): recall@5 = 0.66 overall; MRR = 0.41
- rwd-embed-1024 (quantized): recall@5 = 0.76 overall; MRR = 0.52
- Category drift seen in 'Seasonal Apparel' — recall@5 dropped ~9% vs catalog baseline (older snapshot).

Notes: full notebook + neighbor inspection links are in the Drive folder (shared above). Quantization hurt absolute cosine separation slightly in rare categories; we added a column with cosine delta in the CSV.

Next recommended step: run a focused 200k SKU pass for Seasonal Apparel and compare index configs (HNSW vs IVFPQ).

Marissa

- Ballpark cost for the 200k SKU run (compute + index rebuild + embedding generation)?

Sofia — thanks, good questions. Quick answers and next steps: 

Cost / timeline (rough estimate) for 200k run:
- Embedding generation: ~6–8 GPU-hours (T4 equivalent) for 200k at 1024-d; estimate $X (we'll provide exact once we size infra).
- FAISS rebuild (HNSW/IVFPQ tuning): ~2–4 CPU-hours; storage/temp costs depend on config.
- Total pilot cost estimate (compute + storage + engineer time): I’ll put a formal quote in the HubSpot deal by EOD.

Pricing tiers (prod 1024d vs 384d):
- 384d baseline: lower per-token/per-embed unit price; faster indexing and smaller storage.
- 1024d: ~2.5x unit cost (storage + compute) — but higher semantic fidelity in tough categories.

Recommended rollout pattern (hybrid):
1) Start with 384d for catalog-wide indexing.
2) Identify top 10% categories by error/regression (we can run the classifier on the eval CSV).
3) For those categories, create a separate 1024d index or tag results for reranking with 1024d embeddings (dense rerank).
4) Monitor cost/quality trade-offs for 30 days; automated fallback to 384d when latency spikes.

Compliance / docs: we’ll attach SOC2 and standard security pack to the HubSpot deal.

Next steps I will take today:
- Put a formal scoped quote into HubSpot (ACME-2026-EMB-12).
- Schedule the 200k run once you approve the quote and share the sample CSV.
- Share a rollout plan doc with recommended index configs and cost estimates.

If that works I can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to finalize scope.

—
